title: Repeated triggers reuse the same digest output filename

evidence.quote:
if date is None:
            date = datetime.utcnow()

reasoning: POST /trigger allows a new job after the previous one completes, but the persisted digest filename and the EPUB writer both use only date plus period. Two manual triggers on the same day write the same output path, so the later job can overwrite the earlier digest file while both database rows still exist. The generator also recomputes the date at compile time instead of using the created Digest row, so a job crossing midnight can write a different filename than the one stored on the digest record.
recommendation: Make the output filename a stable per-digest value, such as including the digest UUID or a full timestamp, and pass that filename or creation date into the EPUB/PDF generation path instead of recomputing it. Ensure completed digest rows point to the actual generated file.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature lists no linked tests, and repository search found digest download tests but no POST /digests/trigger test that starts two same-day jobs or checks stored filename versus generated path.
suggestedRegressionTest: Create two completed manual digests on the same UTC day through the trigger/generation path and assert they receive distinct filenames and both files remain downloadable; add a boundary test where the digest creation date and EPUB generation date differ.
minimumFixScope: Bindery digest creation, EPUB/PDF filename generation, and a focused trigger/download regression test.
